cohort: Pregnant rats were exposed to either a low PM2.5 dose via intratracheal instillation or an equivalent volume of normal saline (controls).
finding: PM2.5 exposure in pregnant rats resulted in increased absorbed blastocysts, lower maternal weight gain and fetal weight, increased blood mononuclear cells, platelets, and IL-6 levels, and placental pathological changes including thrombus and chorioamnionitis, suggesting placental inflammation and hypercoagulability but not oxidative stress.
followup_time: 24 hours after the last intratracheal instillation
birth_weight: Lower fetal weight found in PM2.5 exposure group.
gest_age: Exposure at pregnant day 10 and day 18; cesarean section 24 hours after the last instillation.
